item.title: DOJ defends White House media ban, urges court to reject lawsuit
item.description: The Department of Justice defended President Trump's recent media ban, arguing that reporting by CNN, MS Now and Politico on a wide range of issues jeopardized national security and spread falsehoods.
item.content:encoded:
The Department of Justice defended President Trump's recent media ban, arguing that reporting by CNN, MS Now and Politico on a wide range of issues jeopardized national security and spread falsehoods.

(Image credit: Finn Gomez)
item.dc:creator: NPR Staff

item.title: Major news outlets banned by Trump will have their day in court
item.description: CNN, MS NOW, and Politico are asking a federal judge to hold the president in check for what they say is a violation of their Constitutional rights simply because he doesn't like how they cover him.
item.content:encoded:

item.title: There's growing concern that Trump may deploy the National Guard ahead of elections
item.description: Fears are growing that President Trump may deploy the U.S. military to polling places in the upcoming elections, despite strict state and federal laws against such a move.

item.title: Poll: Most voters agree the 2026 midterms are all about Trump — and they disapprove
item.description: A new NPR/PBS News/Marist poll finds President Trump — and his unpopularity — is an outsize factor in why most voters say they want Democrats to win the midterms.
item.content:encoded:

item.title: In Utah, trails are being adjusted to allow adaptive bikes better access
item.description: New technology, including electric motors, means disabled people can get out on mountain trails. But those trails need to be modified to make them friendly for hand-cycles or three-wheeled ebikes.

item.title: Trump administration to remove 760,000 Affordable Care Act enrollees over fraud claims
item.description: White House officials allege these individuals were fraudulently enrolled in the program or do not exist. Vice President Vance said the move would save $2.2 billion.

item.title: How abuse in some of Tennessee's juvenile prisons remained under wraps
item.description: Employees at a group of privately-run juvenile detention facilities across Tennessee failed to report suspected physical and sexual abuse to the state, and were allegedly discouraged from calling 911.
